To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the combination of two systems improves performance on Subtask B and (2) both systems perform best with features specific to social media.

(1) the use of dictionaries and stylistic information is crucial to the performance of sentiment detection systems on social media data; (2) combining the output of two sentiment detection systems can improve performance; and (3) the performance of sentiment classification systems can be further improved by using a combination of features, including dictionary features, stylistic information and linguistic features

(1) dictionaries developed specifically for social media are useful for sentiment detection; (2) stylistic features are useful for sentiment analysis, particularly for social media; (3) the use of dictionaries and stylistic feature improves performance over the use of only dictionaries, and (4) the use of both systems together improves results over either system alone
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of sentiment analysis tools that are tailored for social media and that are capable of detecting the polarity of individual subjective phrases.
the development and evaluation of sentiment classification techniques that are tailored towards online genres and are robust across different types of data.
the development of supervised sentiment detection models for online genres and the application of these systems to SemEval2014.
